title: Cases of Airline Pilots Consuming Alcohol or Drugs before Boarding Aircraft in Singapore
what_it_is: Cases of Airline Pilots Consuming Alcohol or Drugs before Boarding Aircraft in Singapore

sections.label: CAAS pilot alcohol rule
sections.summary: CAAS requires Singapore carriers to ensure pilots consume no alcohol at least eight hours before flight worldwide.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Specifically, CAAS requires Singapore carriers to ensure that their pilots do not consume any alcohol at least eight hours before flight, wherever they operate in the world.

sections.label: Alcohol offence penalty and records
sections.summary: The offence carries up to $100,000 and/or five years' imprisonment, and CAAS records show no pre-boarding alcohol or drug cases in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Doing so is an offence under the Air Navigation Order and carries a penalty of up to $100,000 and/or five years' imprisonment upon conviction.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Based on records from CAAS, there has not been any case of pilots consuming alcohol or drugs before boarding aeroplanes in Singapore.

sections.label: CAAS reviewing deterrence regulations
sections.summary: CAAS is reviewing regulations and procedures to more strongly deter such behaviour.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: CAAS is reviewing the regulations and procedures to more strongly deter such behaviour.

sections.label: Bottle to throttle and ramp inspections
sections.summary: Carriers must instruct pilots to abstain eight hours before flight; there is no random blood testing, but over 900 CAAS ramp inspections since 2013 found no intoxication signs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Right now, under the Air Operator Certificate requirements, Singapore carriers have to instruct the pilot to abstain from alcohol consumption at least eight hours before flight, in what we call bottle to throttle time.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: There is currently no random blood testing conducted in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: However, there are spot checks specifically performed by CAAS during ramp inspections.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: And so far, CAAS has conducted over 900 such ramp inspections since 2013 and has not detected any pilot showing signs of alcohol intoxication.
